decisions.title: Separate Companies for Each Business
decisions.decision: 4up, Services, 4eye, and 1game will all be separate companies
decisions.reasoning: Cleaner branding, separate focus areas, easier to sell/spin off individually. Each has distinct value propositions and target audiences.

alternatives.option: Single umbrella company with all products
alternatives.reason: Individual products have clearer market positioning when separate
Even paired products have distinct enough value props to warrant separation

decisions.title: Launch Order: 4up → Services → 4eye/1game
decisions.decision: Launch 4up first, then Services ~2-3 days later, then 4eye/1game
decisions.reasoning: Services provides income faster, funds development, and is low effort after 4up because 4up content powers the Services website. 4eye/1game require more complex architecture.

alternatives.reason: Need revenue faster to fund development; 4up/Services are quicker wins
Not feasible with available time and resources

decisions.title: Services Launch in Phases
decisions.decision: MVP (landing + contact + about) in 2-3 days, Phase 2 (checkout, accounts) in 3-5 more days, Phase 3 (component store) in 1-2 weeks
decisions.reasoning: Breaking into phases allows faster time-to-market while still building toward full vision. MVP can start generating leads immediately.

alternatives.reason: Speed to revenue is more critical than feature completeness

decisions.title: Primary Target: EDU Youth Market
decisions.decision: Focus on capturing youth into brand funnel as primary target, with mass-market products (4up, Services) funding the EDU vision
decisions.reasoning: The 'everyone' angle is too easily replicated. EDU market capture requires specialized knowledge and quality that's hard to replicate. However, mass-market products fund the longer-term EDU play.

alternatives.reason: Differentiation comes from specialized EDU focus; mass-market is means to an end
